title: Book 8 — Urania, Chapter 107
paragraphs: When Xerxes had entrusted his sons to Artemisia to take back to Ephesus, he called Mardonius and bade him choose from the army whom he wanted, and make his deeds, if possible, correspond to his words. So matters went that day. In the night, on the king's command, the commanders of the fleet began to withdraw their ships from Phaleron to the Hellespont, each as quickly as he could, to guard the bridges for the king to cross. As the barbarians sailed near Zoster, seeing the small points of rock that stretch out to sea from this part of the mainland, they took these for ships and fled for some distance. At length, perceiving that they were not ships but rocky points, they regrouped and continued their voyage.
